filename: The Impact of Sub‐Grid Heterogeneity on Air‐Sea Turbulent Heat Flux in Coupled Climate Models.pdf
title: The Impact of Sub‐Grid Heterogeneity on Air‐Sea Turbulent Heat Flux in Coupled Climate Models
code_availability: https://github.com/ocean-transport/scale-aware-air-sea (archived at https://zenodo.org/records/15615679) and aerobulk-python package at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11205116
testbed_rationale: Provides open, cloud-optimized (ARCO/Zarr) high-resolution coupled model fields and diagnostic sub-grid air-sea heat flux datasets explicitly intended to motivate and benchmark sub-grid air-sea parameterization development.
pain_points: High-frequency snapshot data were not archived, necessitating offline bulk formula calculations using daily-averaged outputs
Atmospheric and oceanic fields reside on distinct spatial grids requiring horizontal regridding and colocation
Lack of global, high-resolution coupled observational datasets covering both ocean and atmosphere simultaneously
Strong non-linearities in bulk coupling formulas make scale-separation sensitive to filter scale and formulation
extraction_notes: The paper does not train machine learning models, but quantifies the sub-grid air-sea heat flux term Q* that is missing in coarse climate models and serves as a direct parameterization target for climate models and scientific ML.
